update_log: Complete exhaustive baseline of major historical monuments, ancient structures, and iconic temples of India for Static GK.

monuments_and_temples.name: Brihadisvara Temple (Tanjore)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Great Living Chola Temples'; entirely built of granite; features a massive vimana (temple tower) and a monolithic Nandi statue.

monuments_and_temples.name: Sun Temple, Konark
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Conceived as a colossal chariot of the Sun God with 24 intricately carved stone wheels drawn by 7 horses; famously known as the 'Black Pagoda'.

monuments_and_temples.name: Kailash Temple, Ellora (Cave 16)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: The world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure, carved from the top down out of a single volcanic basalt cliff face.

monuments_and_temples.name: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
monuments_and_temples.key_features: One of the oldest structural stone temples in South India, overlooks the Bay of Bengal; part of the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram.

monuments_and_temples.name: Khajuraho Temples
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Famous for its erotic sculptures and Nagara-style shikhara towers; the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is the largest and most prominent in this group.

monuments_and_temples.name: Dilwara Jain Temples
monuments_and_temples.key_features: A complex of five marble temples globally renowned for their extraordinarily intricate and delicate white marble ceiling and pillar carvings.

monuments_and_temples.name: Sanchi Stupa
monuments_and_temples.key_features: One of India's oldest stone structures; houses relics of Lord Buddha; famous for its beautifully carved gateways (Toranas) depicting Jataka tales.

monuments_and_temples.name: Hampi Monuments (Virupaksha Temple)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Ruins of the medieval capital city of Vijayanagara; features the functional Virupaksha Temple, the Vittala Temple with its iconic Stone Chariot, and musical pillars.

monuments_and_temples.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Expanded significantly by the Nayak Kings
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Dedicated to Meenakshi (Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva); famous for its 14 towering, colorful gopurams decorated with thousands of mythological figures.

monuments_and_temples.name: Ajanta and Ellora Caves
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Satavahana, Vakataka, Chalukya, and Rashtrakuta Dynasties
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Ajanta features 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves famous for fresco paintings; Ellora features 34 caves representing Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism coexisting harmoniously.

monuments_and_temples.name: Gol Gumbaz
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Mausoleum housing Adil Shah's tomb; features one of the largest domes in the world unsupported by pillars; contains the famous 'Whispering Gallery'.

monuments_and_temples.name: Taj Mahal
monuments_and_temples.key_features: White marble mausoleum built in memory of Mumtaz Mahal; incorporates Persian, Islamic, and Indian styles; universally celebrated for its symmetric layout and pietra dura inlay work.

monuments_and_temples.name: Qutub Minar Complex
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, completed by Iltutmish (Delhi Sultanate)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: The world's tallest brick minaret (73 meters); the complex also contains the 4th-century iron pillar of Chandragupta II, famous for its rust-resistant composition.

monuments_and_temples.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Built when the capital shifted from Agra to Shahjahanabad; constructed from red sandstone; historic seat of power where the Prime Minister hoists the national flag on Independence Day.

monuments_and_temples.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Designed by Frederick William Stevens (British Raj Era)
monuments_and_temples.architectural_style: Victorian Gothic Revival & Indian Traditional Architecture
monuments_and_temples.key_features: An architectural blending of late 19th-century European structural ideas with traditional Indian palace crafts; serves as a major railway headquarters.

monuments_and_temples.name: Victoria Memorial
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Designed by William Emerson (British Raj Era)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: A large marble building built using white Makrana marble (the same quarry as the Taj Mahal); dedicated to the memory of Queen Victoria.

monuments_and_temples.name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Originally built by Ashoka, rebuilt in brick during the Gupta period
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Marks the location where Siddhartha Gautama (Lord Buddha) attained enlightenment under the sacred Bodhi Tree.

monuments_and_temples.name: Sun Temple, Modhera
monuments_and_temples.key_features: Features a magnificent rectangular stepped tank called the 'Ramakund' lined with over 100 miniature shrines; no active worship takes place here today.

monuments_and_temples.name: Kamakhya Temple
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Rebuilt by Chilarai (Koch Dynasty) and Ahom Kings
monuments_and_temples.key_features: One of the oldest and most revered Shakti Peethas in India, dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya; central hub for Tantric practices; hosts the annual Ambubachi Mela.

monuments_and_temples.name: Lingaraja Temple
monuments_and_temples.built_by_dynasty: Somavamsi Dynasty (with later additions by Ganga rulers)
monuments_and_temples.key_features: The largest temple in Bhubaneswar ('The Temple City'); dedicated to Harihara (a combined form of Vishnu and Shiva); features a dominant deula tower.
